mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the head and spine to the trunk was most worthwhile because it showed nerves and blood reaching the same muscles, connecting several earlier ideas.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the digestive and urinary organs into their named slots felt predictable, even though it helped place them in the body.

surprise.text: The joined trunk showed that the diaphragm separates the chest from the abdomen while nerves, vessels and the food pipe cross between regions.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary: the named slots and matching anatomical routes made the placements understandable.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if another chapter explored how the assembled systems work together. The final cutaway tied them together, though much of this chapter was straightforward placement.
